releases.name: ANet 0.3.8
releases.body:
Release date: 2026-10-22.

| Component | Version | Repository |
|---|---|---|
| ANetCore | v0.16.1 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetCore |
| ANet (`anet`) | v0.3.8 | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANet |
| ANetHub (`anet-hub`) | v0.3.3 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetHub |
| ANetLink | v0.2.0 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetLink |

Documentation: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/

## Upgrading

0.3.8 is a patch release. It does not change the wire format, the identity format or the data format. A 0.3.7 node and a 0.3.8 node work together, and the hubs need no upgrade. Update a node with `anet update` and restart its daemons. The plugins for coding agents move to version 0.3.0, their final version; a plugin 0.3.0 works with anet 0.3.7 or later, and plugins 0.1.x and 0.2.0 keep working with anet 0.3.8.

## Changes

### The MCP server brings the node up
- `anet mcp` starts the node of the selected identity when no daemon answers and the data directory is set up. It starts the daemon exactly as `anet up` does (detached, with the same checks, and without sending the control token to a port that another process holds), in the home directory of the user rather than in the working directory of the session, and waits up to 20 seconds for it. Two sessions that start at the same moment start one daemon. Everything it reports goes to standard error; standard output carries only the MCP session.
- When the node cannot run, `anet mcp` serves anyway instead of exiting with status 1. Every tool is listed; `guide` works as before; `node_status` answers `running: false` with the reason code, the sentence and, in `next`, the command that fixes it; every other tool answers with the same reason as a tool error; and the instructions of the server begin with it. The server looks for the daemon again at each call, so the tools work in the same session once the node runs.
- The reasons are existing codes: `daemon_not_running`, `daemon_not_answering`, and the code of a refusal of the data directory or the configuration (for example `config_key_removed`). A data directory without a node gets the new sentence key `daemon_not_running.not_set_up` and the command `anet up` (`anet --id <name> up` for a named identity). `anet mcp` does not create an identity itself: it starts with every session of a coding agent, and a misspelt identity name in a plugin setting must not create and start a new identity.
- `anet mcp` starts only the identities of the anet home of the user (`~/.anet` and `~/.anet/ids/<name>`), and no node whose configuration enables the `shell` module. A data directory that `ANET_DATA_DIR` or `ANET_HOME` names elsewhere, for example one of a workspace whose variables the host passes on, and a node with the `shell` module, are started with an explicit `anet up` (sentence keys `daemon_not_running.outside_home` and `daemon_not_running.shell_enabled`). A daemon that already runs is used in every case.
- What `anet mcp` tells the model names the reason and the command and no path: the data directory, the files of a refusal and the log of the daemon appear only in its error output (sentence keys `daemon_not_running.mcp` and `daemon_not_answering.mcp`; `daemon_not_running.not_set_up` no longer names the data directory).
- `anet mcp` with the `mcp` module turned off in `config.json` still refuses with `module_absent` and exit status 2.
- The guide tells the agent to answer a question about anet itself ("what can anet do") by calling `node_status`, showing the real state of the node and offering concrete next actions, and to run `anet up` when `node_status` names it.

### Plugins for coding agents
- The plugins move to version 0.3.0, their final version. Enabling a plugin is enough to install anet and run its node: when the MCP launcher finds no anet executable and the setting `anetPath` is empty, it runs the official installer without arguments (`install.sh` on Linux and macOS; on Windows the do

Release date: 2026-10-22.

| ANet (`anet`) | v0.3.7 | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANet |
| ANetHub (`anet-hub`) | v0.3.3 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetHub |
| ANetLink | v0.2.0 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetLink |

Documentation: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/

## Upgrading

0.3.7 is a patch release. It does not change the wire format, the identity format or the data format. A 0.3.6 node and a 0.3.7 node work together, and the hubs need no upgrade. Update a node with `anet update` and restart its daemons. The plugins for coding agents move to version 0.2.0, which reads the guide of the installed anet; a plugin 0.2.0 needs anet 0.3.7 or later.

## Changes

### The guide for coding agents
- New command `anet guide [<topic>] [--list]` and new MCP tool `guide` (parameter `topic`). Both return the guide of the installed release for coding agents: `overview` (the default: the tools, delegation, answering tasks, payments, and requests written as `@anet`), `setup` (starting the node, joining a hub, verification) and `status` (reporting the state of the node). An unknown topic is answered with the list of topics; `anet guide` exits with status 2 for it. The command needs no running node, and the tool makes no call to the daemon.
- The command name, the tool name, the parameter and the three topics are permanent. The guide text changes with each release and takes precedence over instructions bundled with a plugin or a skill.
- The guide explains requests that a user addresses to the network by writing `@anet …`: find the agent with `list_agents` and `get_agent_card`, prefer an agent marked official or whose card verified, use its capability with `send_message`, and report the reply as another party's text. The skill that `anet agents wire` installs carries the same text.
- `anet mcp` has 15 tools.

### Plugins for coding agents
- The plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy, OpenCode, ZCode, Google Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Trae and DeepSeek Harness move to version 0.2.0. Each plugin contains a launcher of `anet mcp`, a short skill that tells the agent to read the tool `guide` of the installed anet and follow it, a `/anet` entry point where the host supports one, and the setup that installs anet with the user's consent. The plugins name no tools and no features, so later releases of anet reach every tool without a new plugin version.
- The plugins run on Windows. Each host starts the launcher in the way its own process creation supports: a `.cmd` launcher found through `PATHEXT` for hosts that resolve commands as cross-spawn does, a Node launcher for Google Antigravity, and the absolute path of the `.cmd` launcher for Trae. The runner has a Windows counterpart with the same settings, the same search for the executable (including the installation directories of `install.ps1`) and the same refusals.
- The releases of the Gemini CLI extension carry `win32.anet.tar.gz` next to the archives for Linux and macOS, so `gemini extensions install` uses a release archive on Windows too.

### Wiring Trae and ZCode
- `anet agents wire trae` writes the MCP server entry into the user configuration of Trae and Trae CN (`User/mcp.json` in the application data directory of each product, on Linux, macOS and Windows) and the short persona into `~/.trae/user_rules/agentnetwork.md` (`~/.trae-cn/user_rules/` for Trae CN), applied to every session. Every file is backed up first; `unwire` restores them.
- `anet agents wire zcode` installs the anet plugin through the ZCode command-line program (`zcode plugins marketplace add` and `zcode plugins install anet@agentnetwork`) and checks the result; `unwire` removes it. ZCode reads MCP servers only from plugins, so anet writes nothing under `~/.zcode`. Without the command-line program, the command prints the two steps

Documentation: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/

Installing on Linux and macOS: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/intro/install.html#intro-install-script

## Upgrading

0.3.6 is a patch release. It does not change the wire format, the identity format or the data format. A 0.3.5 node and a 0.3.6 node work together, and the hubs need no upgrade. Update a node with `anet update` and restart its daemons. On Linux and macOS, the installation command is now the single line `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh | sh`: the installer starts the node and joins `https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn` itself, so `anet up` and `anet hub-register` no longer follow it. A script or an agent that must not join a hub passes `--no-join`. The section `Upgraded from anet <version>` is now in the installation log, not in the output. `ANET_INSTALL_BASE` now replaces every download source of `anet update` instead of being tried first. See "Upgrading to 0.3.6" in the documentation.

## Changes

### Windows installation
- Download sources. `install.ps1` installs exactly the release it was published with, so every source is asked for that version. The npm mirror `registry.npmmirror.com` (the tarball of the npm package of the build) and the GitHub release of the project are probed in parallel, for at most 3 seconds each and 4 seconds in all; the sources that answered are tried first, the faster one first. Then `registry.npmjs.org`, jsDelivr, and last `agentnetwork.org.cn` and `hub.agentnetwork.org.cn`. A source that does not serve the release (no answer, an HTTP error, a page instead of a file, a missing file, another version) is passed over for the next one. A source only determines where the files come from: a file that fails the release pins or the signature check ends the installation, whichever source served it. The npm tarball is read in memory, and a tarball with an entry name that is not a plain relative path is refused whole. A GitHub download may be redirected only to `github.com` and `*.githubusercontent.com`. `-Base` and `ANET_INSTALL_BASE` replace the sources, as before.
- Output. The installer prints one line per phase and a short summary: whether anet is installed and running, the node's AID in full, the hub and whether the node joined it (or the `anet-hub admit` command for the hub's operator), the agent given remote control with `-Controller` and the command that revokes it, one line when an earlier installation was taken over, a `Note:` line only for something left to the user, and last `Details:` with the path of the log of the run. On an interactive console, the download is one line updated in place with a bar, the size, the speed and the time remaining; `NO_COLOR` turns its colours off, and the bar falls back to ASCII when the console code page cannot show it. Without an interactive console, the download is reported in one line. With `ANET_LANG=zh...`, the summary is in Chinese.
- Log. Everything else (the sources probed and tried, each check, every takeover step, the `PATH` and `Run` value changes, and the output of `anet init`, `anet up`, `anet doctor` and `anet hub-register`) is written to `%USERPROFILE%\.anet\logs\install-<UTC time>.log`, in a directory with the private access control list; when the data directory is not ready (a refusal, or data of an earlier release left in it), to `%TEMP%\anet-install\`. A refusal or a failure is one `Error:` line followed by the `Details:` line; the exit statuses 0, 1 and 3 are unchanged.
- Without `-Controller`, the line now also starts the node, joins `http

| ANetLink | v0.2.0 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetLink |

Documentation: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/

Installing on Windows: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/intro/install.html#intro-install-windows

## Upgrading

0.3.5 is a patch release. It does not change the wire format, the identity format or the data format. A 0.3.4 node and a 0.3.5 node work together, and the hubs need no upgrade. Update a node with `anet update` and restart its daemons. On Windows, running the installation command again also updates an installation and reuses its directory when that directory passes the checks. The installer no longer asks a confirmation for `-Controller`: a script or document that relied on that confirmation as a second step now grants access as soon as the command runs. On Linux and macOS, running the `install.sh` command again replaces AgentNetwork 1.x, anet 0.1 and anet 0.2 in the same run; see "Upgrading" in the documentation.

## Changes

### Windows installation
- The installation is started with one line, identical in `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, PowerShell 7, `bash` and `zsh` in WSL 1 and WSL 2, and Git Bash:

  ```text
  powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol=3072; & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm -UseBasicParsing https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.ps1))) -Controller CONTROLLER_AID"
  ```

  Without `-Controller CONTROLLER_AID`, the line installs the default build only. The placeholder is a plain word because `cmd.exe` reads `<` and `>` as redirections, and the installer refuses it unchanged. Run in WSL, the line installs the Windows build on the Windows host, for the Windows user; `install.sh` installs inside the Linux distribution. WSL interoperability, which is enabled by default, must be available.
- The installer asks nothing and reads nothing from the console. `-Controller` on the command line is the consent to the grant, and the console confirmation of 0.3.4 is removed. At the end, the installer prints what was granted, read back from `config.json` and `peers.allow`, and the two steps that revoke it. The installation completes without a console, as in the tool call of an agent, a CI job or WSL interoperability.
- The exit status of `powershell.exe` is the result of the installation: 0 when everything was done; 3 when ANet is installed but the installation stopped before its last step and the commands that complete it were printed; 1 for a refusal or a failure before anything was installed; otherwise the exit status of the `anet` command that failed. Run in an open PowerShell window, the script leaves the window open and sets `$LASTEXITCODE`.
- An elevated window is no longer refused, and `-Elevated` is accepted without effect. ANet is installed for the current account with its own directories, `PATH` and `Run` value. While Windows has a standard user token for the account (User Account Control on), no program of the account is run from the elevated window: an earlier `anet.exe` is classified by its contents, and its `stop` command and `npm` are printed instead of run. The node is started through a one-time Task Scheduler task with the interactive token and the least privileges, so that neither it nor the controller's commands run with the elevated token; when the task cannot run or does not complete, the node is not started: it starts at the next logon through the `Run` value, and the installation ends with exit status 3 and the commands to run in a normal window. releases.name: ANet 0.3.4
releases.body:
Release date: 2026-10-20.

| Component | Version | Repository |
|---|---|---|
| ANetCore | v0.16.1 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetCore |
| ANet (`anet`) | v0.3.4 | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANet |
| ANetHub (`anet-hub`) | v0.3.3 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetHub |
| ANetLink | v0.2.0 (unchanged) | https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetLink |

Documentation: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/

Installing on Windows: https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/intro/install.html#intro-install-windows

## Upgrading

0.3.4 is a patch release. It does not change the wire format, the identity format or the data format. A 0.3.3 node and a 0.3.4 node work together, and the hubs need no upgrade. Update a node with `anet update` and restart its daemons; the data directory, the identity and the configuration are kept. An installation from npm is updated with `npm update --global @agentnetwork/anet`.

One check changes on Linux and macOS: `anet doctor` reports the recovery file under `identity.recovery` only when another account can read it, so a recovery file with mode 0400 is no longer reported. On Windows, `anet` is installed with the PowerShell script `install.ps1`.

## Changes

### Windows
- `anet` runs natively on Windows 10 version 1809 or later and on Windows Server 2019 or later, on amd64 and arm64, in the default build and in the build with the `shell` module. WSL2 is not required.
- The PowerShell script `install.ps1` installs `anet` with Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7 and no other tool. The script is signed (`install.ps1.sig`) and carries the SHA-256 digests of the four Windows builds. A downloaded binary must match its digest, and then verifies the signed release manifest itself, before anything is installed. The installer refuses an elevated window unless `-Elevated` is given, checks that the installation directory is private to the user, adds it to the user's `PATH` and starts the node at logon through the `Run` value of the user. With `-Controller <AID>` it installs the build with the `shell` module, gives exactly that AID access to it after one confirmation on the console, and joins `https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn` unless `-Hub` is given.
- The daemon keeps its data in `%USERPROFILE%\.anet` and its runtime files in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\anet\run`. Private files and directories carry an access control list that admits only the user, `SYSTEM` and `Administrators`. Secrets are private from the moment they are created, and files are opened without following reparse points. `anet up` starts the daemon detached from the console; it runs as the logged-on user and never as a Windows service.
- The `shell` module runs commands with Windows PowerShell by default; `pwsh`, `cmd` and the absolute path of a supported interpreter can be configured. A command runs as a process tree in a job object and ends as a whole. An argument that contains one of the characters `" % ! ^ & | < > ( )`, a carriage return or a line feed is refused, because a batch file would interpret it again.
- `anet update` replaces a running `anet.exe` by renaming it aside, puts it back when a later step fails, and removes the copies that were moved aside on a later run.
- `anet pull` marks received files as downloaded from the Internet (`Zone.Identifier`) and adds the suffix `.txt` to names on which Explorer acts, such as `.lnk`, `.url`, `.scf` and `desktop.ini`.
- Auto-reply has no sandbox on Windows and refuses every run that needs one. It also refuses an agent program that is a batch file.
- Backends on a Unix socket, TCP backends on the same host, the `p2p` module and the ANetLink sockets are refused with a reason, because the node cannot identify the process at the far end. Backends on another host over HTTPS work.
- The installation, shell, sandbox and security pages, the READMEs and `SECURITY.md` describe the Windows build in English and Chinese.

### Distribution
- Each release is published on npm. `@agen
